concepts.title: Checking Proportion by Cross Multiplication
concepts.definition: Two ratios a : b and c : d are proportional exactly when the cross products agree: a times d must equal b times c; Viswanath's 6 : 3 idli batter matches Puneet's 4 : 2 because both cross products give 12.
concepts.formula: cross_ad = a * d; cross_bc = b * c
concepts.key_idea: One cross multiplication settles proportionality: 6 x 2 = 3 x 4 = 12.

concepts.title: Map Scales and Representative Fraction
concepts.definition: A map's representative fraction such as 1 : 6000000 fixes the ratio of map distance to ground distance, so 1 cm on the map stands for 6000000 cm or 60 km on the ground; multiplying the measured map distance by the scale and converting centimetres to kilometres gives the geographical distance.
concepts.key_idea: 1 cm with RF 1 : 6000000 covers 60 km; scale up the measured centimetres.

concepts.title: Ratios with More than Two Terms
concepts.definition: A ratio can chain three or more linked quantities, like the spice mix 8 : 4 : 2 : 1 of coriander, chillies, dal and fenugreek; keeping the taste same means every term changes by one common factor, and a known term fixes the unit part for all the others.
concepts.key_idea: Halve the chillies and every other ingredient halves too: 8 : 4 : 2 : 1 :: 4 : 2 : 1 : 0.5.

concepts.title: Dividing a Whole in a Given Ratio
concepts.definition: To split a whole among ratio terms, divide the whole by the sum of the terms to get one part, then multiply each term by that part; 110 units of concrete in the ratio 1 : 1.5 : 3 needs 20, 30 and 60 units because one part is 110 divided by 5.5.
concepts.key_idea: One part first, then scale every term: 110 in ratio 1 : 1.5 : 3 gives 20 : 30 : 60.

concepts.title: Pie Chart Angles from Shares
concepts.definition: A pie chart divides the full 360 degrees of a circle in the ratio of the data shares; a grade with 12 of 40 students takes 12/40 of 360 degrees, so each slice angle equals the share divided by the total, times 360.
concepts.key_idea: Grades 12 : 10 : 8 : 6 : 4 of 40 students cut the circle into 108, 90, 72, 54 and 36 degrees.

concepts.title: Inverse Proportions (Speed and Time)
concepts.definition: When one quantity grows by a factor while the other shrinks by the same factor, they are inversely proportional and their product stays constant: speed times time locks in the fixed distance of 90 km, so doubling speed halves the travel time.
concepts.key_idea: Speed 5, 15, 30, 60 km/h take 18, 6, 3, 1.5 hours - every row multiplies to 90.

concepts.title: Direct Proportion (Rule of Three)
concepts.definition: For a direct proportion a : b :: c : d the missing fourth term is d = bc/a; more bricks need more workers in the same ratio, so 18000 bricks need 20 workers when 4500 bricks need 5.
concepts.textbook_ref: hegp203.txt lines 371-390 (rule of three, workers and bricks example)

solution_steps.explain: b times c forms the numerator of the rule of three.
Dividing by a yields the missing fourth term.
